limits.evidence: Lines 147-151: the backdrop-dismiss handler fires on any click whose target is the dialog and whose coordinates fall outside its rect. With a mouse, pressing on the expanded native seek bar or volume slider, dragging past the dialog edge and releasing over the backdrop produces a click on the common ancestor (the dialog) with outside coordinates. That calls closeVideo() and pauses the video while the user is scrubbing.
limits.fix: Record the pointerdown target, e.g. a ref set in onPointerDown to event.target === event.currentTarget plus an outside-rect check. In onClick, only call closeVideo() when both pointerdown and click happened on the backdrop.

limits.evidence: expandVideo (lines 36-49) calls shell.close() and shell.showModal() with no feature check. HTMLDialogElement.showModal needs Safari 15.4 or later. On older engines inside a default Vite 'modules' build target (Safari 14 to 15.3), clicking the preview or Expand video throws a TypeError. The inline video has no controls (controls={expanded}), so the tutorial can't be played there. The written instructions still work, so the task is not blocked.
limits.fix: Guard with `typeof shell.showModal === 'function'`. If it's missing, either skip expansion and render the inline video with controls, or note in the release record that the supported browser floor is Safari 15.4 or later.

limits.evidence: beforeEach assigns HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal and close directly (lines 5-7). vi.restoreAllMocks() only reverts vi.spyOn, so these overrides persist for the rest of the file and in any run with isolation turned off. In the default per-file isolation they are harmless, but they hide whether jsdom's own dialog implementation, if it has one, behaves differently.
limits.fix: Save the original descriptors and restore them in afterEach, or use vi.spyOn(HTMLDialogElement.prototype, 'showModal') with mockImplementation, defining the method first if jsdom lacks it.
